places.name: The Loom Temple
places.epithet: The great ring of woven light
places.text: At the city's heart, open to the sky at its apex, stands the temple that houses the great ring of woven light from which the Weave takes its name. Loomwardens pace its circumference, adjusting sigils and murmuring complex formulae. From here winds are redirected over Emberweave's dust, storms are delayed to spare the northern harvest, and the weather over Caer Veyn's harbor is kept, barely, within limits the harbormasters can tolerate. Guarded stairways climb from it to the Aerialring.

places.name: The Skyward Towers
places.epithet: Three tall spires rooted firmly in stone
places.text: The anchors of Skyloom: they house the anchor-runes, lift-wards and harassed clerks whose task is to make sure the sky-bound part of Skyloom stays attached to the rest. From The Crown, one reaches the Aerialring by way of them.

places.name: The Tower Plazas
places.text: The plazas round the roots of the Skyward Towers, at the city's west end.

places.name: The Lift-Seal Office
places.epithet: No seal, no lift
places.text: Where lift-seals are issued: the permits without which nobody rides the Skyward Towers up to the Aerialring.

places.name: The Warden's Court
places.epithet: Where the Weave Warden holds court
places.text: The seat of the Weave Warden of Skyloom, elected from among the senior Loomwardens, at the edge of the tower plazas.

places.name: The Veil Court
places.epithet: Open to the sky above and The Crown beyond
places.text: A broad, reflective plaza at the city's eastern end. Here treaties concerning sky-lanes over the Union, the extension of weather wards over the other Weaves, and the limits of certain magical experiments are read aloud and bound.

places.name: The Windspire Lift
places.epithet: A discreet arch at the Court's edge
places.text: An invisible column of rising air that carries those with the proper seals up to the Aerialring.

places.name: The Skyward Gate Docks
places.epithet: Where skycraft sidle in along glowing mooring-rings
places.text: Against the northern wall. Couriers from Northreach, diplomatic cutters out of Caer Veyn, and merchant vessels that prefer thin air to crowded roads all put in here. Heavier craft put down instead at Farwatch Landing on the coast.

places.name: The Luminous Ward
places.epithet: Light treated more as a guest than a resource
places.text: A district of pale houses and glass-roofed courtyards spreading west and south. Mirrors, thin stone and cleverly angled panels (most of them fired in Midhurstnes) pull dawn and dusk deep into interior rooms. Wind-chimes and wire-songs hum between balconies, giving the whole ward a faint, constant music.

places.name: Stormwatch Edge
places.epithet: Many oaths are taken here; a few are not survived
places.text: A simple stone terrace with a simple stone rail out from the eastern wall, looking toward The Crown's western wall and, beyond it, the slow, silent churning of the Everstorm that rings the heart of the Union.

places.name: The Walls
places.epithet: Low walls and open terraces
places.text: The city's edges are ringed by low walls, towers under slate cones, and open terraces.

places.name: The Loom Stores
places.epithet: Cheese, liquor, and a great many candles
places.text: Where the Aerialring's needs are gathered before being sent up: cheese, liquor, and a great many candles.

places.name: The Cloudwine Distilleries
places.epithet: Drunk mostly by people who have just come down
places.text: Distilleries that make cloudwine, a clear, cold spirit.

places.name: The Loom Road
places.text: East through the Loomward stormgate to The Crown.

places.name: The Sapphire Road
places.text: West through Midhurstnes, Castfield and Clitford toward Cloudmoor Harbor.

overlays.name: Aerialring
overlays.epithet: Floating above the Groundring, for the winged and the very trusted

places.name: The Aerialring
places.epithet: It belongs to whatever has learned to trust the sky
places.text: The higher, thinner loop over the Groundring: open galleries, high aeries and Sky Lanes, reserved mostly for the winged and the very trusted. It is reached by the Windspire Lift or through guarded stairways in the Loom Temple. Wing-guards enforce three simple rules: no reckless flight near docks, edges, or the Sky Lane beacons; no tampering with lift, gravity, or wind without proper sigils; and no duels over open Everstorm.

places.name: The Halo Overlook
places.epithet: For vows expected to outlive everyone present
places.text: A circular platform of translucent stone at the Aerialring's exact centre, suspended directly above the Loom Temple's inner ring. From here one can look down through crystal at the Loom itself, and beyond that to the fields of the Shadowline, a faint pattern of roads and threads barely visible through spell-glass. It is used sparingly: for flight-rites, public auguries, and vows whose consequences are expected to outlive everyone present.

places.name: The Temple Stairways
places.epithet: Guarded
places.text: The guarded stairways that climb from the Loom Temple below: with the Windspire Lift, the way up to the Aerialring.

places.name: The High Aeries
places.epithet: On the western and eastern flanks
places.text: Home to elves of the upper air, aarakocra scouts, harpies who have traded shriek for discipline, and certain tieflings and Sangrith bearing rune-bound wings.

places.name: The Loft Market
places.epithet: A compact cluster of stalls
places.text: In the northern section: feathersteel harness and flight-cloaks (Castfield leather, Waringley wool), instruments that measure altitude, pressure, and cloud-depth, and small vials of carefully stored, highly unstable weather.

places.name: The Windspire Lift
places.epithet: No seal, no lift
places.text: The invisible column of rising air from the arch at the Veil Court's edge comes up here, carrying those with the proper seals.

places.name: The Dropway
places.epithet: When falling becomes flight, and when it does not
places.text: To the south a clear shaft of air opens toward the hills below. Young fliers are taught here, under supervision, precisely when falling becomes flight and when it does not. Those who learn the lesson incorrectly are buried at Buneymouth.

places.name: The Sky Lanes
places.epithet: Paths in the air marked by dim rune-light
places.text: The lanes along which winged patrols fly. The lamps that mark them over the countryside below are tended from the ground, by the candle-makers of Aillenestre and Fercelle.
